_readme: NOT FOR AUTOMATED IMPORT. This is a candidate-data artifact for a human to walk through manually via /admin/ (sources.html -> materials.html -> claims.html) or a separately-reviewed one-off script, cross-checking each row against methodology-seed-v1.md's human review notes first. Field names match supabase/migrations/00029_methodology_knowledge.sql's actual columns. Local string keys (source_key/material_key) stand in for real uuids, which don't exist until a human actually creates these rows - nothing here has been inserted into any methodology_* table. Every claim is implicitly review_status=candidate, active=false (the schema has no human_verified column - human review state lives in review_status/reviewed_by/reviewed_at, all null here).

claims.extracted_text: Athletes produce more force and sequence more efficiently when focusing externally on movement outcomes rather than internally on body movements.
claims.observable_evidence: Coaching instructions directed at ball flight trajectory/target outcome rather than a specific body segment during live or cage swings.
claims.applies_when: Delivering verbal feedback during batting practice, cage work, or game preparation.
claims.does_not_apply_when: Conducting explicit body-awareness drills or physical therapy screenings where internal focus is intentionally required.
claims.coaching_cue: Focus on ball flight trajectory and where you want to hit the ball rather than internal body movement.
claims.quality_notes: Gemini reports on-screen citations (Wulf 2010, Wu 2012, Castaneda & Gray 2007) - plausible given real external-focus-of-attention research literature, but NOT independently confirmed by a human watching the video. Confirm before trusting research_supported.

claims.extracted_text: The human body self-organizes to accomplish tasks within an environment, so coaches should manipulate environmental/physical constraints rather than over-cueing mechanics verbally.
claims.observable_evidence: Use of environmental constraints (step-behind drills, variable overload/underload bats) to induce mechanical adjustment without explicit verbal mechanics instruction.
claims.applies_when: Designing practice environments to correct hitting mechanics and timing faults.
claims.does_not_apply_when: An athlete lacks basic movement patterns or physical mobility required for the constraint.
claims.quality_notes: Reviewer downgrade from Gemini's strong_candidate: this is a coaching/practice-design principle, not cleanly an observable-from-video mechanical claim.

claims.extracted_text: Early hitting is usually caused by loading too early, which causes moving forward too early, early hip extension, and lunging at the ball.
claims.observable_evidence: Hitter shifting weight forward well before pitch release, back hip extending early, body posture lunging toward the ball.
claims.applies_when: A hitter is consistently early on pitches and lunging forward into contact.
claims.does_not_apply_when: A hitter is late on pitches or failing to initiate stride in time.
claims.quality_notes: Explicit causal chain (early load -> forward move -> hip extension -> lunge), which is coaching heuristic, not independently validated - human should decide whether to preserve as causal or soften.

claims.extracted_text: Extension after contact keeps the barrel through the tunnel toward the pitcher, maximizing power and helping direct the ball rather than rolling over into weak grounders.
claims.observable_evidence: Bat barrel path continuing forward toward the pitcher after contact with extended arms prior to the finish roll-over.
claims.applies_when: Executing swing follow-through and extension on pitches through the middle of the zone.
claims.does_not_apply_when: Adjusting to extreme inside pitch locations where hand path must clear tightly.
claims.coaching_cue: Drive the barrel through the tunnel from home to the pitcher.
claims.quality_notes: sport_scope reviewer-downgraded from Gemini's 'both' to 'softball' pending human confirmation of baseball transferability.

claims.extracted_text: Hitters must rotate the torso to bring the pipe around to the tee, avoiding diving the chest forward at the ball.
claims.observable_evidence: Maintaining spinal posture during torso rotation, chest not lunging forward toward the ball, across different tee locations.
claims.applies_when: Working on swing plane control, torso rotation, and pitch location adjustment.
claims.does_not_apply_when: Full game situations where timing and stride dynamics vary unpredictably.
claims.coaching_cue: Rotate around your center so the pipe comes to the tee—don't dive your chest forward.
claims.quality_notes: Coaching cue is an explicit internal-mechanics instruction - see contradiction_group vs DRV1-001/DRV1-002.

claims.extracted_text: Hitters move back and forth between three different plate locations to learn how swing timing and tempo need to adjust for pitch distance.
claims.observable_evidence: A hitter taking swings sequentially from three different home-plate markers at varied distances from the front-toss screen.
claims.applies_when: Practicing timing rhythm and reaction-time adjustments during front toss or live pitching practice.
claims.does_not_apply_when: Isolating stationary swing mechanics on a tee where pitch arrival time is not a factor.
claims.quality_notes: Very short source clip (~28s) - likely excerpted from a longer lesson; source itself recommended as candidate-level trust, not approved_for_scope, until more material is reviewed.

claims.extracted_text: When setting up a tee, pitch location dictates contact-point depth relative to the body (away off lead hip, middle off front foot, inside in front of front foot) to maintain connection.
claims.observable_evidence: Positioning of the batting tee relative to the hitter's front foot/lead hip across different pitch locations.
claims.applies_when: Setting up batting-tee drills for specific pitch-location practice.
claims.does_not_apply_when: Practicing dynamic pitch recognition or live-pitching hitting without controlled tee setups.
claims.coaching_cue: Outside off lead hip, middle off lead foot, inside out front.

claims.extracted_text: Jumping back into a med-ball toss teaches lower-half loading into the back hip while keeping weight inside the back knee to ground forces effectively.
claims.observable_evidence: Hitter jumping back onto the rear leg, hinging at the back hip without the knee collapsing outward, before throwing the medicine ball.
claims.applies_when: Developing dynamic lower-half loading and back-hip weight distribution.
claims.does_not_apply_when: Players lack basic lower-body balance or have joint issues requiring physical screening.
claims.coaching_cue: Jump back and load into your back hip.
claims.quality_notes: Medicine-ball weight guidance (2-4 lbs) for young players is a good concrete youth-safety detail.

claims.extracted_text: Our core philosophy is to be on time for his best fastball; when hitters truly believe they are on time for the best fastball, it opens up their entire offensive execution.
claims.observable_evidence: Not cleanly observable from ordinary swing video - a stated mental-approach philosophy, only weakly inferable from timing consistency over many at-bats.
claims.applies_when: Standard plate appearances across all counts.
claims.does_not_apply_when: Situational at-bats where sitting on a specific offspeed pitch is explicitly called.
claims.coaching_cue: Be on time for his best fastball.
claims.quality_notes: POSSIBLE FUTURE APPROACH-KNOWLEDGE DOMAIN - not swing mechanics; concept mapping to 'timing' is a forced fit into the current mechanics-only taxonomy. Reviewer-downgraded from Gemini's strong_candidate.

claims.extracted_text: To alleviate outcome pressure, hitters must reverse-engineer success from outcome results back to winning individual pitches.
claims.observable_evidence: Not observable from swing video - a mental self-evaluation framework claim.
claims.applies_when: All game at-bats and practice routines.
claims.does_not_apply_when: Gemini reported 'never' - flagged as needing a human to supply a real exception before this is approval-ready.
claims.quality_notes: POSSIBLE FUTURE APPROACH-KNOWLEDGE DOMAIN. does_not_apply_when needs a real answer, not 'never'.

claims.extracted_text: Hitters who roll over on their front foot lose 8% of energy transfer through the front foot and 11% through the backside.
claims.observable_evidence: Video observation of the front foot rolling onto its lateral edge during or immediately following contact (qualitative pattern only - the numeric figures are not independently observable/verifiable).
claims.applies_when: During the weight-transfer, foot-plant, and rotation phase of the swing.
claims.does_not_apply_when: Evaluating post-finish relaxation or non-swing movement.
claims.coaching_cue: Maintain pressure through the inside of the lead foot and big toe during rotation.
claims.numeric_evidence_ref: Chad Miller's own spoken claim in a podcast interview; no on-screen citation of methodology, sample size, or a checkable published source. Do NOT approve as stated without independent verification.
claims.quality_notes: STRONGLY RECOMMEND SPLITTING into (a) the qualitative front-foot-rollover pattern (reasonable candidate) and (b) the 8%/11% figures (should stay unapproved / likely_reject pending real evidence). Reviewer-downgraded from Gemini's strong_candidate.

claims.extracted_text: Hitting a baseball is a transfer of kinetic energy derived from the ground up, delivered sequentially through hips, shoulders, hands, and bat barrel while keeping the barrel behind the ball.
claims.observable_evidence: High-speed video showing sequential rotation: ground drive, lead-hip turn, trunk rotation, hand acceleration, barrel delivery.
claims.does_not_apply_when: Executing check swings, bunts, or emergency contact swings.
claims.coaching_cue: Drive from the ground up through hips, shoulders, and hands.
claims.quality_notes: General, uncontroversial proximal-to-distal sequencing description - much safer than SCI-001. Consider softening 'universal' framing.
